cases.subject: Lumen
observations: Lumen alpha retry tests committed one payment for three requests sharing an idempotency key.
Lumen beta retry tests replayed the original payment receipt after a lost response.
cases.counterexample: Lumen gamma retries with new idempotency keys committed duplicate payments.
cases.claim: Lumen idempotency keys prevent duplicate payments in the measured retry tests.
cases.conclusion: Lumen payment retries should reuse the original key and unchanged payload.
cases.applicability: Lumen alpha and beta payment requests with retained idempotency keys only.
cases.assumption: The request payload and idempotency-key scope remain unchanged.
cases.paraphrase: How should Lumen resend a payment after losing its reply without charging twice?
cases.missing: What is Lumen's approved retention period for payment retry keys?

cases.subject: Meridian
observations: Meridian alpha queries used fewer database reads after adding an indexed customer filter.
Meridian beta queries preserved all matching customers when the indexed filter preceded the result limit.
cases.counterexample: Meridian gamma queries lost matching customers when the customer filter was applied after the result limit.
cases.claim: Meridian indexed customer filters preserve matching records before limiting in the measured queries.
cases.conclusion: Apply Meridian customer filters before the result limit.
cases.applicability: Meridian alpha and beta queries with the measured customer index only.
cases.assumption: The measured predicate and index definition remain unchanged.
cases.paraphrase: Where should Meridian restrict customers so a small result window does not hide valid matches?
cases.missing: What is Meridian's maximum supported customer count?

cases.subject: Nova
observations: Nova alpha backups restored the same rows and schema from an exported PostgreSQL snapshot.
Nova beta backup verification detected a missing relationship after comparing restored record fingerprints.
cases.counterexample: Nova gamma row counts matched despite altered restored relationship data.
cases.claim: Nova snapshot fingerprints detect restored data changes that equal row counts miss.
cases.conclusion: Verify Nova restored rows and schema fingerprints instead of relying only on counts.
cases.applicability: Nova alpha and beta PostgreSQL snapshot fixtures only.
cases.assumption: Capture and dump share one exported snapshot and deterministic record ordering.
cases.paraphrase: How can Nova tell whether a recovered database contains the original records rather than just the same number?
cases.missing: What is Nova's contractual recovery time objective?

cases.subject: Prism
observations: Prism alpha cancellation tests dropped pending provider work before database storage began.
Prism beta cancellation tests preserved the original receipt when the database commit had already completed.
cases.counterexample: Prism gamma cancellation after a sent commit could not prove that the write was rolled back.
cases.claim: Prism cancellation stops pending work but does not establish rollback after a sent commit.
cases.conclusion: Reconcile Prism uncertain writes with the original request key.
cases.applicability: Prism alpha and beta cancellation fixtures with retry-safe requests only.
cases.assumption: The client retains the original request arguments and key.
cases.paraphrase: Can Prism assume a cancelled request never saved data when commit may already have been sent?
cases.missing: What is Prism's measured remote provider cancellation delay?

cases.subject: Helix
observations: Helix alpha session tests expired at the expected boundary after converting TTL seconds to milliseconds.
Helix beta session tests preserved valid sessions before the same millisecond expiry boundary.
cases.counterexample: Helix gamma sessions expired early when TTL seconds were added directly to a millisecond timestamp.
cases.claim: Helix session expiry requires consistent millisecond units in the measured tests.
cases.conclusion: Convert Helix TTL seconds before adding them to millisecond timestamps.
cases.applicability: Helix alpha and beta session expiry fixtures only.
cases.assumption: The timestamp remains in milliseconds and the supplied TTL remains in seconds.
cases.paraphrase: How should Helix calculate session expiry when the lifetime and clock use different units?
cases.missing: What is Helix's approved default session lifetime?

cases.subject: Cobalt
observations: Cobalt alpha agents retrieved another agent's scoped memory when no author filter was supplied.
Cobalt beta agents excluded unrelated project memories by supplying the agreed project scope.
cases.counterexample: Cobalt gamma agents missed another contributor's lesson when they filtered recall to their own agent ID.
cases.claim: Cobalt shared recall needs a project scope without an unnecessary author filter in the measured handoffs.
cases.conclusion: Use the agreed Cobalt project scope and omit the author filter for shared lessons.
cases.applicability: Cobalt alpha and beta agents in the same trusted deployment only.
cases.assumption: Project scope and agent IDs are provenance filters rather than authorization boundaries.
cases.paraphrase: How can Cobalt find a colleague's project lesson without mixing in unrelated projects?
cases.missing: Which Cobalt agent has administrative authorization?
